_doc: Vũ Linh Đường lineage (rules-proposals R5). Re-leaned Metal, Water -> Wood, Fire in place: its seat (372, grassland: Wood 35.6 %, Fire 22.9 %, Earth 22.5 %, Metal 10.3 %, Water 8.7 %) holds almost no Metal or Water, and no Metal-Water land lies within reach of Thu Trì. Bronze is the hall's craft (luyện khí, trận pháp), not its root: it casts with charcoal fire and hangs its bells in living trees. Outer gate: charcoal-burners-primer (proposal, Yellow, Fire or Wood). Inner gate and above: canopy-bell-canon (proposal, Profound, Wood). Secret arts: molten-bronze-litany (proposal, Fire, inner gate) and listening-bell-seal (proposal, Earth tier, Wood; elders and the head). Unpriced.

lineage.tree_route_note: Bells that ring before the blow: Willow Dance and Bending Willow for the canopy bells' evasion, Bamboo Flute for the tuned bronze that resists soul and charm.

techniques.name: Charcoal-Burner's Primer (Thiêu Thán Quyết)
techniques.concept: The foundry's first method. Outer disciples burn the hall's charcoal in earth kilns and work the bellows for the pour, and the primer is learned at the kiln mouth: draw the wood's qi as it chars and the fire's qi as it rises, and hold the heat even for a day and a night. A disciple who can keep a kiln steady can keep a casting fire steady, and a bell is only as good as its pour.

arts.concept: A stance: the holder's linh lực regenerates faster while they stay Composed; their next Fire art after leaving it deals more damage.

techniques.lore: Written by the founder Chung Thiết Liên in 930, when he brought his lamp-casters south and had to make charcoal before he could make bells (V149).

techniques.name: Canon of the Bells in the Canopy (Lâm Linh Kinh)
techniques.concept: The hall's canon and its art of warning. A bell is hung in a living tree, and the cultivator's Wood qi joins it to the tree's roots. When the bell rings, the roots carry the note to every other tree in the line and to the cultivator's feet. A line of rain bells across a forest is a single array that hears. In a fight the canon hangs small bells in the air around the holder: they warn of every strike before it lands, and their ringing slows and confuses a foe.

arts.concept: Gains a Bell charge for the fight; each bell raises evasion a little and rings to reveal the unseen foe, and each new bell reserves a little more linh lực than the last.
Rings every hung bell at once: the foe is slowed and takes light Wood damage per bell.
A passive: the first strike each fight against the holder while a Bell charge is held is warned and partly evaded.

techniques.lore: Chung Thiết Liên's canon, completed by Chung Tàn Hưởng in 1080 and given its ninth layer by Ân Thanh Linh in 1105, the year the hall hung its first bell line over the forest road (N-vu_linh-02).

techniques.name: Molten Bronze Litany (Dung Đồng Kệ)
techniques.concept: The casters' fighting art. The litany is sung at the pour to keep the bronze running, and the same breath throws a gout of molten bronze from the hand. It burns and then hardens: a foe struck often enough is encased and slowed. Inner disciples learn it at their first pour and are scarred by it at their second.

arts.concept: A Fire strike of molten bronze that leaves a burn and a bronze stack; at three stacks the foe is slowed.

arts.new: Hard as a Bell (Kiên Như Chung)
arts.concept: Spends the foe's bronze stacks to raise the holder's ward for a few seconds, by stack.

techniques.lore: The founder brought it from the lamp foundries of Thanh Đăng Trấn, where it was a work song before it was an art.

techniques.name: Seal of the Listening Bell (Văn Linh Ấn)
techniques.concept: How to cast a bell that hears. The caster seals a thread of Wood qi into the bronze at the pour, tuned to one thing: a footstep, a charm, a voice, someone listening at a door. The bell rings only for that. In a fight the seal turns the holder's ward into a listening bell: it rings a moment before each art the foe casts, and the holder may answer first.

arts.new: It Rings for You (Vị Quân Minh)
arts.concept: Marks one foe: for the fight, the holder's ward rings a moment before each of that foe's arts, and the holder's next art against them is cast at once.
A passive: the holder's bells and wards resist soul and charm arts, and each charm they stop rings and slows its caster.

techniques.lore: Ân Thanh Linh's art, first used in 1030 for the bell she cast the Nhiếp family at twenty, which rings only when someone listens at a door. She has taught it to no one in full.
